did_you_know.text: Did you know? Joash became king when he was only seven years old. He reigned in Jerusalem for forty years, and his mother was Zibiah of Beersheba.

Did you know? The text emphasizes that Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest—a wording that highlights the central connection between his leadership and Jehoiada’s influence.
Did you know? Jehoiada arranged for Joash to marry two women, and they had sons and daughters.
Did you know? Joash instructed the priests and Levites to collect money annually from all the cities of Judah to repair the Temple, but at first the Levites did not hurry to carry out the task.

Did you know? According to the text, the sons of Athaliah had broken into the house of God and used the sacred objects there in the worship of the Baals. This condition of the Temple provided the background for Joash’s restoration initiative.
Did you know? Joash ordered a chest to be made and placed outside the gate of the house of the LORD so that the people could put their contributions for the Temple into it.

Did you know? Whenever the chest was full, the Levites brought it before the king. The king’s secretary and the chief priest’s official emptied it and returned it to its place, allowing a large amount of money to be collected regularly.

Did you know? The contribution money was used to hire stonemasons, carpenters, and workers skilled in iron and bronze. The repairs restored the house of God to its proper condition and strengthened it.
Did you know? Jehoiada died at the age of 130—a remarkably advanced age according to the account in this chapter.
Did you know? Jehoiada was buried in the City of David with the kings—not because he was a king, but because he had done good in Israel, for God, and for God’s house.

Did you know? After Jehoiada’s death, Joash and the officials of Judah abandoned the house of the LORD and turned to the worship of the Asherah poles and idols. Zechariah son of Jehoiada tried to bring them back to the way of the LORD, but they would not listen.

Did you know? Zechariah son of Jehoiada was murdered in the courtyard of the house of the LORD at King Joash’s command. The text connects this act with Joash’s failure to remember the kindness Jehoiada had shown him.
Did you know? The Aramean army was small in number, yet the LORD delivered Judah’s much larger army into its hands. The text explains this by saying that Judah had abandoned the LORD.
Did you know? After the Arameans withdrew, Joash’s servants conspired against him and killed him in his bed. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
Did you know? The text names the two conspirators against Joash: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite.
Did you know? After Joash died, his son Amaziah became king in his place, and the rule of the house of David continued.
